class.name: MetaHumanHairSimulator
class.brief_description: Simulates a MetaHuman groom's guides and moves its hair meshes with them.
class.description: Simulates a groom's guide curves every frame and moves the hair meshes in [member hair_meshes] with them. Each frame it writes how far every guide point is from where skinning alone would put it into a small texture, which the hair materials' vertex shaders read: every rendered strand, and the hair shell, follows its two guides, so the cost is that of the guides (about 20 000 particles for a MetaHuman) however dense the hair is drawn. The solver is position-based and steps at a fixed rate of [code]60 * substeps[/code] steps per second, so it behaves the same at any frame rate. It keeps segment lengths, pulls toward the groomed shape (from [member root_stiffness] at the root to [member tip_stiffness] at the tip, so the style holds while the ends move), and pushes the hair out of the [MetaHumanHairSimulation]'s colliders. The groom was styled under gravity, so the hair is first settled at rest and offsets are measured from there: idle hair keeps exactly its groomed shape. Each hair mesh gets its own copy of its materials, so several instances of a character move their hair independently. The MetaHuman importer creates this node for the scalp hair when [code]metahuman/hair/dynamic[/code] is on.

method.name: get_max_offset
method.description: Returns the largest distance, in meters, between a guide point and its rest position this frame.

method.name: get_mean_offset
method.description: Returns the mean distance, in meters, between the guide points and their rest positions this frame.

method.name: reset
method.description: Snaps the hair back to its rest shape, for example after teleporting the character.
